title: Every line with its time checked
prompt: An audit needs every line of the log file, with broken lines and impossible times flagged rather than lost. Write `solve(application_logs_raw)` so it returns each line's id, time and level, and the raw text of every line that didn't fit.
rules: The starter saves the log file. Return `log_id`, `logged_at` (a timestamp), `level` and `bad_record` (text), in that order.
One row per line that has text on it; empty or blank lines give no row. Keep repeated lines.

A line that isn't a valid JSON record has NULL fields and the line exactly as it arrived in `bad_record`. A record whose `logged_at` isn't a valid timestamp is flagged the same way, but its `log_id` and `level` are still read.
A missing field is just NULL, and the record isn't flagged. A good record has a NULL `bad_record`.
hints: Keep every line with the default mode, add `bad_record STRING` to the schema and name it in `columnNameOfCorruptRecord`.
With `logged_at TIMESTAMP` in the schema, a time that doesn't parse makes the record malformed.
Try the starter's file with a record like `{}` or one without `level` before deciding they're bad.
starter:
def solve(application_logs_raw):
    path = "/tmp/logs/export"
    application_logs_raw.write.mode("overwrite").text(path)
    # Read the file at `path` and return every line with log_id, logged_at, level and bad_record.
    return application_logs_raw
explanation: This is the flagging read from the lesson with a typed time: `spark.read.json(path, schema="log_id STRING, logged_at TIMESTAMP, level STRING, bad_record STRING", columnNameOfCorruptRecord="bad_record")`. In the default `PERMISSIVE` mode every non-blank line becomes a row. A line that isn't JSON, or is JSON but not a record, such as `null`, keeps its text in `bad_record` and NULL everywhere else. A record whose time is `yesterday` or 31 April is valid JSON but doesn't fit the schema: Spark still reads its `log_id` and `level`, sets `logged_at` to NULL and keeps the raw line. A record with no `level`, or even `{}`, fits the schema, so it isn't flagged. Blank lines are skipped. Reading `logged_at` as text would miss the impossible times, and `DROPMALFORMED` would lose exactly the lines the audit wants.
